meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why was Owen given a zero, and who decided it?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. And the basis for it?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Kids draft elsewhere and paste it in. Did you speak to Owen before the zero, as 4.1 requires?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and stays quiet. You didn't answer me: did you speak to Owen before you entered the zero?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
I'm reading it. Kids misquote; that's a bad quotation, not proof of who wrote the essay. What else is there?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Fine. The quote isn't in the scene. What do you want done about it, and on what authority?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
People change their thesis between an outline and an essay. That's called revising. Show me why this one isn't.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. He'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. I want it in writing tonight with nothing on his file, and the rest goes in my email.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth. I'll confirm it with Owen tonight, so put the time and the room in your email, Hale.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday the twelfth, under procedure 4.4, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require that confirmation in writing with the time and room, and I still require an answer on whether you spoke to Owen before entering the zero. I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she accepted a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth under 4.4, replacing the zero with nothing on his record, and she still wants it in writing tonight with the time and room and Owen's confirmation of the day. That is the fair outcome, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You showed the quote that appears nowhere in the scene and answered her misquote defence with a plain fact, which left her nothing checkable to argue with.
What cost ground: You never answered whether you spoke to Owen before entering the zero, so she asked twice and it stayed open as a procedural grievance.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history, with its late-night edits the night before the essay was due, came close to that night. It proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether you had spoken to Owen before the zero, answer it in one plain sentence before moving on, so that grievance never gets a second airing.
